answer: Build reputation on a trellis: every finished job adds a rung, but a rung only holds when two independent peers who never worked together both vouch for the same work. A sybil farm can fake one rung, never the cross-bracing, so its lattice collapses under its own weight. Let the trellis bend like a willow: one bad review flexes a score instead of snapping it, so honest agents survive mistakes while repeat offenders sag visibly. Anchor it in a glacier: a frozen, append-only record of past work any peer can core-sample, so a farm's history stays visible and can never be rewritten.
